$comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Loom community-JSON specification version.
Every document under docs/references/ declares, in its YAML frontmatter, the spec version it was
written against. A doc whose declared version differs from `current` below is STALE and must be
re-verified before the Skill is allowed to rely on it. See _meta/publishing-flow.md.
Three layers are versioned independently, because they change at different rates. See
_meta/versioning-policy.md for what each governs and when to bump it.
statusReason: PROVISIONAL, not frozen. Phase A.5 now parses the engine-native experience schema (v2), registers
its definitions, and seeds its instances into one shared runtime engine per extension. It is not yet
rendered by the running app; the generic card through live UI gates are Phase A.6-A.10. Phase A
ends in a deliberate human review gate whose EXPECTED outcome is that this specification changes.
Do not treat any version number here as stable until Phase A's gate closes and this file's status
flips to `stable`. Until then, docs in this tree describe an intended contract, verified against
the engine's parser and evaluator and the app-shell parser, but not yet end-to-end in the running UI.

resolvedQuestions.$comment: Open questions settled by reading the source, recorded so they are not re-litigated.
resolvedQuestions.stringLiteralsInFormulas: RESOLVED 2026-07-14: string literals ARE supported, in both single and double quotes (formula_evaluator.dart:540). "availabilityState == 'available'" is valid. This was previously listed as an unknown.
resolvedQuestions.unaryNotOperator: CORRECTED 2026-07-17: `negationOperators` below previously claimed BOTH `!` and `!=` are absent. Verified directly against the parser: only `!=` is actually absent (`_comparison()`, formula_evaluator.dart:428-436, never checks for it). Unary `!` genuinely works -- parsed by `_unary()` (:458-462) and evaluated (`!_bool(v)`, :236). `formulas.md` corrected to match.

resolvedInGrammar.$comment: Gaps that were in knownGaps and are now fully closed -- grammar, engine execution, AND validator coverage all confirmed. Moved here 2026-07-16 per the publishing flow (_meta/publishing-flow.md step 8), rather than deleted, so the resolution is traceable.
resolvedInGrammar.transitionInputs: GAP-1, RESOLVED 2026-07-16. `transitions[].inputs` + `{input.x}` interpolation + `renderBindings[].repeater.itemActions` are implemented and validated. Real engine execution confirmed: `applyTransition` accepts `inputs`, refuses when a `required` one is missing, and `{input.x}` resolves inside effects (including recursively in nested List/Map effect values) -- proven end-to-end by `tournament-ballot.cast-vote` in the frozen Tabletop Club JSON (two concurrent-shaped calls with different `choice` values produce two distinct, non-racing `tournament-vote` rows). Validator adds `unknown_input_type`, `unknown_input_reference`, `unknown_item_reference`. See `app/packages/core/loom_workflow_engine/lib/src/models/workflow_models.dart` (`LoomWorkflowTransition.inputs`, `RepeaterSpec`/`RepeaterItemAction`), `effect_evaluator.dart` (`{input.x}`), `local_workflow_engine_api.dart` (`applyTransition`'s required-input check).
resolvedInGrammar.queryBackedSources: GAP-4, RESOLVED 2026-07-16. `instanceDataSchema[].source` (`query(type where foreignField == localField)`) is now genuinely parsed (`source_query.dart`) AND executed: `_hydrateSourceFields` runs the bounded equality query against the real store and populates the field with full matched-row instance data, wired into every read path that materializes instance data for a caller (`queryInstances`, `availableTransitionsAsync`, `applyTransition`'s result, `dueNotifications`). Proven end-to-end: `tournament-ballot.ballots` (source-backed) now populates for real, and its already-existing, unchanged formulas (`voteCounts`/`winner`/`tiedCandidates`/`isTie`) compute correctly over it. Also required implementing `{id}` interpolation (the acting instance's own id) -- a related, previously-undiscovered gap the frozen JSON's `cast-vote` effect (`"ballotId": "{id}"`) depended on but nothing implemented; see `effect_evaluator.dart`/`local_workflow_engine_api.dart`. Validator adds `invalid_source_query_syntax`, `dangling_source_query_workflow_type`, and widens `computed_field_written_by_effect`/`computed_field_seeded` to also cover `source`-backed fields (previously only checked `formula`).
resolvedInGrammar.styleFieldBinding: RESOLVED 2026-07-24 (CALR.9b, commit f4bf58f). `RenderBinding.styleField` now genuinely parses (mirrors `audienceMemberField`'s pointer-field pattern) and the App Shell genuinely consumes it: `stylePaletteFrom(accent)` derives six related-but-distinct colors from one community accent via systematic HSL hue rotation, and a single shared `_calendarEntryStyleColor` resolver reads `instanceData[binding.styleField]` to index that palette for the Calendar agenda row's fill and the month-grid/week-strip event-title dot -- falling back to the flat accent for any binding that doesn't declare `styleField`. Proven end-to-end on the real frozen fixture: Friday game night (`cardStyleId` 2) and Summer tournament (`cardStyleId` 1) render in genuinely distinct, accent-derived colors. Independently verified: 118/118 App Shell + 141/141 engine tests, 0 analyzer issues. Moved out of `proposedNotImplemented` (was stale there) per this file's own rule that the code wins on disagreement.

envelope.governs: The install wrapper: packageId, communityId, communityHandle, displayName, extensionId, branding, seedDataFiles, experience.

experience.governs: How the experience block declares workflows.

values.1: LEGACY shallow form. Flat workflows[] cards (workflowId/title/entryText/actionText/resultText/calendar?/responseChoices?) plus one bespoke top-level block per special feature. Cannot express a state machine, guard, effect, or formula. This is what the app loads today; the seven non-Tabletop communities still use it. Not recommended for new communities.
values.2: ENGINE-NATIVE form. workflowDefinitions (real state machines) + workflowInstances (seed data), parsed by LoomWorkflowStateMachine.fromJson and executed by LocalWorkflowEngineApi. This is the target and what all docs in this tree describe.

grammar.governs: The grammar of each workflowDefinitions entry: states, transitions, guards, effects, renderBindings, instanceDataSchema, formulas.

values.1: Original renderBindings grammar. A member-create affordance was a single flat `creatable` object on a binding (byPersonaIds/label/prefill).
values.2: BUMPED 2026-07-21. `creatable` is replaced by an `actions[]` array on a binding: archetype-owned actions, each with kind/label/byPersonaIds and optional workflowType/scope(tab|instance)/presentation(fab|button)/prefill. Generalizes creation into a scope+presentation model (tab-scoped FABs vs instance-scoped card buttons / contextual FABs) and is the extension point for future non-create action kinds. See render-bindings.md (`actions`) and proposedNotImplemented.actionsGrammar below.

groundedIn.$comment: The code this specification is derived from. If any of these change, this spec may be stale.

knownGaps.$comment: Capabilities the docs describe as needed but the grammar does NOT yet support. Each must be closed or explicitly deferred before the Skill (Phase 3) can rely on this spec. GAP-1 and GAP-4 moved to `resolvedInGrammar` above, 2026-07-16.
knownGaps.instanceCreation: GAP-2 (LARGELY RESOLVED 2026-07-21). Grammar/model + tab-scoped UI are done. Grammar v2 (2026-07-21) replaced the flat `renderBindings[].creatable` object with an `actions[]` array (see grammar layer values.2 and proposedNotImplemented.actionsGrammar). Tab-scoped `create` actions are fully built and shipping end-to-end: `event-rsvp` (New event, CALR.3-3h2), `tournament-event` (New tournament, CALR.3b), and every other tab-level creation runs through the real generic creation pipeline (GenericWorkflowCreationCard via EngineNativeArchetypeCreationCard's cardSurfaceFamily dispatch), verified by full-suite tests. What REMAINS is the instance-scoped surface (scope: instance -- a card `button` or a contextual FAB, with `{context.*}` resolution from the in-focus/owning instance), tracked in proposedNotImplemented.actionsGrammar and the tracker's CALR.4a-f rows.
knownGaps.listMinusActor: GAP-3 (non-blocking). 'All participants except the actor' is not expressible -- no set-difference effect op. Consequence: thread unread state is a single bool rather than per-persona. Proposed: `setFromFormula` effect op + a `removeAll(list, value)` formula function. Additive. Deferred, non-blocking Phase F capability -- not attempted in Phase A'.
knownGaps.responseModel: The `responseModel: { kind: simpleRsvp }` sugar in V2's Calendar_RSVP design doc is NOT parsed by the engine. RSVP must be modeled with plain transitions + effects + formulas instead.
knownGaps.negationOperators: CORRECTED 2026-07-17 (see resolvedQuestions.unaryNotOperator) -- only `!=` is actually absent from the formula grammar; unary `!` genuinely works. Invert `!=` by restructuring: `if(a == b, false, true)` instead of `a != b`. Confirmed by reading the parser (formula_evaluator.dart:428-436).
knownGaps.rankTopN: `rank` / `topN` named functions are proposed in ComputationModel.md but unimplemented. `sortBy` covers the same need.
knownGaps.powExp: `pow` / `exp` are not implemented (would be required for a true Elo expected-score calculation).
knownGaps.stringConcatenation: Formulas cannot concatenate strings. Use `labelTemplate` (e.g. "{value} seats") for display composition instead.

proposedNotImplemented.$comment: NEW grammar/engine surface designed 2026-07-17 for the Calendar redesign (event-rsvp per-row response table, Day/Week/Month/Pending views, real event creation). Fully specified and written into the frozen JSON + reference docs, but NONE of it is engine- or App-Shell-implemented yet -- tracked separately from knownGaps because these are net-new proposals, not gaps in an existing contract. See docs/references/communities/tabletop-club.md section 11's 2026-07-17 review-log row for the full context and the CAL/AS ticket gap list for implementation scope.
proposedNotImplemented.createInstances: New method on the ABSTRACT WorkflowEngineApi (not Local-only, unlike the existing install-time-only seedInstances) -- atomic bulk-create, needed so an event's per-member event-rsvp-response rows can be created as one real API operation, not N racy individual createInstance calls.
proposedNotImplemented.relatedAggregateGuard: New guard kind 7 (guards.md) -- a live count/sum/etc. over a related table compared to a threshold, evaluated by the caller pre-computing the aggregate via the existing real aggregate() method before the still-synchronous evaluateGuard runs.
proposedNotImplemented.stateReservedColumn: `$state` (formulas.md) -- exposes a query-backed row's own current FSM state to `groupCount`/aggregate functions. Requires `_readAllInstancesOfType` (and therefore `aggregate()` and GAP-4 hydration) to merge in the row's `currentState`, which today only exposes raw `instanceData`.
proposedNotImplemented.subtractHoursFunction: New formula function (formulas.md) -- date arithmetic (subtract an hour count from a date), needed to compute tournament-ballot.dueAt as a real computed field instead of a hand-seeded, driftable value.
proposedNotImplemented.mapGetFunction: New formula function (formulas.md) -- pull one value out of a map (e.g. a groupCount tally) by key, defaulting to 0 if absent.
proposedNotImplemented.responseTableBinding: New render-binding key (render-bindings.md) -- points a calendar-family archetype at its per-member response table generically, instead of the App Shell hardcoding field names.
proposedNotImplemented.filterableFacetsBinding: New render-binding key (render-bindings.md) -- named, labeled, computed-field-backed filters/stats a generic list surface may offer.
proposedNotImplemented.creatableActionExperienceField: NEW 2026-07-20, IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-20/21 (CALR.3g/3h1/3h2/3b). `experience.creatableAction` (community-wide defaults) + `experience.tabCreatableActionStyles` (per-tab override, same cascade shape as theme/tabThemes), each holding two independently-resolving fields: `multiActionStyle` (speedDial/stacked/singleFirst -- how multiple tab-scoped create-actions on one tab lay out) and `presentationStyle` (popup/slideOutBottom/slideOutLeft/slideOutRight -- how the launched creation form presents). `popup` uses the official Flutter-team `animations` package's `OpenContainer` (container-transform motion). All three multiActionStyle values and all four presentationStyle values ship end-to-end and are full-suite tested. As of grammar v2 these fields govern `actions[]` entries with `scope: "tab"` (see values.2). Retained here (not moved to resolvedInGrammar) only because this whole spec file is still `provisional`.
proposedNotImplemented.actionsGrammar: NEW 2026-07-21 (grammar v2), EXTENDED 2026-07-21 with a second action kind. Replaced the flat `renderBindings[].creatable` object with an `actions[]` array of two kinds sharing one shape. `kind: "create"`: `label`, `byPersonaIds`, optional `workflowType` (defaults to the binding's own type; set for the cross-archetype case, e.g. a tournament-event-owned action that creates a tournament-ballot), `scope` (`tab` default | `instance`), `presentation` (`fab` default | `button`), and `prefill`. Scope is the whole model: tab-scoped = brand-new instance, always a tab FAB, no `{context.*}`, visible even with zero instances; instance-scoped = related to a specific instance, renders as a card `button` (context = that card's instance) or a contextual `fab` (context = the in-focus instance via the App Shell's existing focus tracker), needs at least one host instance to appear. `{context.id}` = the host instance's own id; `{context.<field>}` = its instanceData field. `kind: "transition"`: names an already-declared `transitions[].id` (`transitionId`, required) on the binding's own workflow type and gives it a distinguished presentation (fab/button) instead of the automatic button row -- removing only that one transition from the row, leaving every other transition rendering automatically as before. `scope` is fixed to `instance` (a transition always acts on an existing instance); `byPersonaIds`/`workflowType`/`prefill` are inapplicable (the transition's own `guard` and `inputs` remain the sole source of truth for eligibility and target type); use `inputs` (not `prefill`) to pass values into `applyTransition`, which may reference `{context.<field>}` as a self-reference to the instance being transitioned. IMPLEMENTED: scope:tab creates (the tab creatable-action FAB -- see creatableActionExperienceField). NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: scope:instance creates (button + contextual FAB + `{context.*}` resolution + excluding instance-scoped actions from the tab FAB), the entire `kind: "transition"` surface, and the grammar-v2 validator rules (unknown_action_kind/scope/presentation, tab_action_cannot_be_button, dangling_action_workflow_type, dangling_action_transition_id, transition_action_cannot_be_tab_scoped, transition_action_cannot_set_workflow_type/prefill/by_persona_ids, unknown_action_input_reference, duplicate_action_transition_id, create_action_cannot_set_inputs, context_reference_outside_instance_action). Tracked in the tracker's CALR.4a-f rows. See render-bindings.md `actions` section for the full grammar.
proposedNotImplemented.editGuard: NEW 2026-07-24 (workflow-grammar.md `states`). A state may declare `editGuard`, the exact same `WorkflowGuard` type already used by `transitions[].guard` (e.g. `{ "allowedPersonaIds": [...] }`), gating who may use the already-existing `editableFields` mechanism while the instance is in that state. Motivated by a live gap found reviewing Tabletop Club's Calendar tab: `event-rsvp`/`tournament-event` already declare real `editableFields` (title/eventDate/eventTime/location/host/capacity), and the generic instance-editing UI (`GenericWorkflowInstanceCard`) already renders real, type-aware editors for them -- but nothing gates *who* may see those editors, unlike every transition, which is already persona-gated via `guard.allowedPersonaIds`. Reuses the engine's existing guard evaluator; no new formula language or engine concept. IMPORTANT DEVIATION from guards.md's documented "absent guard means anyone, always" semantics: that default applies to the guard TYPE in its normal use (transitions), not to this new call site. The App Shell's check for whether to render editors MUST require `editGuard` to be present (non-null) before evaluating it or showing anything -- an absent `editGuard` means no editing is exposed, not "anyone may edit." Transitions don't need this special case because an undeclared transition simply has no button; `editableFields` has no equivalent "not declared" state once it's non-empty, so reusing the open default here would silently widen permissions the moment `showEditors` flips on. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: `LoomWorkflowState.editGuard` parsing, the App Shell reading it (with the null-means-closed call-site rule above) before rendering `GenericWorkflowInstanceCard`'s editors (currently gated only by a static `showEditors` bool with no persona check at all), and validator coverage. New validator rule (proposed): `dangling_edit_guard_persona` (mirrors however `allowedPersonaIds` is already validated for transitions). Tracked in the tracker's CALR.10 row.
proposedNotImplemented.calendarDateRailBinding: NEW 2026-07-24 (theming.md section 5, Calendar requirements). A community's `theme.calendar.dateRail.entries` may declare an ordered list of small visual pieces to render in the Calendar agenda row's date rail (today hardcoded to exactly two pieces: weekday abbreviation over a circle-highlighted day number). Each entry has a `kind` (`dateToken` -- a small fixed vocabulary of pure calendar arithmetic: `weekdayAbbrev`/`dayOfMonth`/`monthAbbrev`/`year`, none of which can come from a formula since none are community data -- or `formula` -- any expression from the existing computation model, e.g. `count`/`groupCount`, evaluated over the set of instances landing on that day, letting a community show anything expressible as a formula with zero new App Shell code), a `style` (a small fixed set of render primitives: `label`/`circleHighlight`/`badge`), and an optional `colorSource` (`accent`, today's flat behavior, or `styleField`, reusing the CALR.9b style-slot palette so the date rail's color is community-configurable too). Closed-primitives/open-composition split: `kind` and `style` are fixed vocabularies (the same relationship formula *functions* have to formula *composition*), but which entries appear, their data source, their order, and their color are all fully JSON-driven. Omitting `theme.calendar.dateRail` entirely preserves exactly today's behavior (`[{kind: dateToken, token: weekdayAbbrev, style: label}, {kind: dateToken, token: dayOfMonth, style: circleHighlight, colorSource: accent}]`) -- zero behavior change for every community that doesn't opt in. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: any of `LoomCardTheme`/theme-cascade parsing of this key, the App Shell rendering it, or validator coverage (proposed: `dangling_date_rail_formula`, `unknown_date_rail_token`, `unknown_date_rail_style`). Tracked in the tracker's CALR.10 row.
proposedNotImplemented.transitionRelatedEffect: NEW 2026-07-24 (effects.md op 11), from closing out the pinned CAL.WaitlistPromotion investigation. A new effect op letting a transition find a QUERIED set of sibling instances of another workflow type (`relatedQuery`: same `filter` shape as `guards.md`'s `relatedAggregate`, plus `sortKey` and `limit: 1`) and apply a named `transitionId` to the first match after sorting -- closing the one remaining cross-instance gap (`relatedInstance`/cross-instance `set` only write one field on one directly-named instance; `createInstance` only spawns new ones; nothing today can find-and-drive an existing sibling through its own state machine). Motivating case: when a going `event-rsvp-response` row leaves (respond-maybe/respond-declined), promote the oldest waitlisted row to `going` automatically instead of requiring the waitlisted member to notice and manually re-tap. Semantics are a REAL `applyTransition` call, not a bypass -- the target transition's own guard (including its own `relatedAggregate` capacity check) is evaluated fresh at the moment this effect runs, and a guard failure is a silent no-op, not an error. This is what lets the effect be attached unconditionally to every transition that might free a seat, with no separate 'did a seat actually open' formula check -- correctness comes from the target's own guard re-evaluating live. `sortKey` sorts by the named field's live value only, NOT insertion order (instance ids are randomly generated, not time-ordered) -- a workflow needs its own explicit timestamp field (e.g. a new `event-rsvp-response.rsvpedAt`, stamped via `set` on the transition that enters the waitlisted state) for a real FIFO guarantee. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: the `transitionRelated` op itself (engine), any App Shell surface, or validator coverage (proposed: `dangling_transition_related_workflow_type`, `dangling_transition_related_transition_id`, `dangling_transition_related_sort_key`). Tracked in the tracker's CAL.WaitlistPromotion row.
